points.description: First challenge correctly NAMED and DESCRIBED. Acceptable challenges (any from the list): adaptation to topology changes/node mobility (nodes join/leave anywhere, any time); security (easy interception or injection of packets, needing encryption/authentication); medium access control (hidden/exposed/near-far terminals, interference, collisions); QoS (changing topology, imprecise information, noise/occlusion); scalability (unknown number of nodes, growing size/load); heterogeneity (different capabilities, ranges, processing); dependability (consistent, reliable routing); power consumption (battery-powered devices). Needs both a name and a correct description tied to mobile/wireless routing.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if only the name or only the description is correct.

levels.says: Only a valid challenge name is given with no or a wrong/insufficient description, or a correct description without naming it.

points.description: Second, DIFFERENT challenge from the acceptable list above, correctly NAMED and DESCRIBED. Must not be the same challenge as P1 or a rewording of it (e.g. hidden and exposed terminal count as one MAC challenge). Generic claims such as 'it is harder' or challenges that also apply equally to fixed wired networks (e.g. plain 'speed') earn nothing.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if only the name or only the description is correct.

levels.says: Only a valid, distinct challenge name is given with no or a wrong/insufficient description, or a correct description without naming it.

rubric.notes: Two distinct valid challenges are needed, each named and described; each is worth half a mark. Give half of a point's marks if only the name or only the description is right. No marks for repeats of the same challenge or vague statements.
